emails.subject: Grid & Gradient #112 — The quiet return of serif logos
emails.body: Grid & Gradient #112. This week I audited forty rebrands shipped over the past year and one pattern jumped out: the geometric sans-serif era is quietly ending, and retina-density screens killed the old rendering excuse. The one-line takeaway: Serif logos are back because screens finally got sharp enough to render them. See you next Thursday. — Marisol

emails.subject: Peak Week — Larch madness comes early
emails.body: Peak Week, your weekly trail brief. Rangers across the North Cascades are reporting golden needles a full fortnight ahead of the usual calendar, and the high passes are still snow-free. The one-line takeaway: Larch needles are turning two weeks early, so book your October hikes for late September. Boots on. — Tomas

emails.subject: Simmer #86 — Brown butter is a flavor, not a step
emails.body: Simmer #86. I baked the same chocolate chip recipe four times this week changing only the butter, and the nutty batch wasn't even close. The one-line takeaway: Browning the butter first turns an ordinary cookie recipe into a bakery one. Stay hungry. — Priya

notes.title: Weekly Digest — Week of Jul 13
notes.content:
Grid & Gradient: Logos are drifting warmer — expect ochre everywhere by spring.
Peak Week: Midweek permits go unclaimed, so hike on Wednesdays.
Simmer: Salting the pasta water is your only chance to season the noodle itself.
